notes: The acceptance task lookup was built for (task_lookup_work_order.md sections 7.4 and 7.8). Six tasks are created so the one asked about is no longer among the recent few, then it is named only by paraphrase -- no filename, so level 1 cannot answer and the side channel has to. Two things are under test that no stub can settle: whether the model still declares intent="report" this deep into a conversation, and whether the answer that comes back is about the RIGHT task. The hard invariant (a read-only question creates no work) is scored automatically; the answer itself arrives on a second pass with no turn_id, so it is read from the [TASK-LOOKUP] log lines rather than asserted here -- expect_reply_mentions filters by turn_id and would report a failure that is the instrument's, not the system's. The sleeps are load-bearing: the answer deliberately waits for the floor, and the first run of this scenario fired both questions back to back, so neither answer ever got one and the run proved nothing about them.
